title: His father's travels: Chicago with Perez, Robichaux, then Piron
summary: The 1917 Chicago trip with Manuel Perez, return to Robichaux, then Piron's band until 1927.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: pumping more information about your father, but it's a wonderful opportunity for us to hear about him from the best possible source. Anything else about the bands he played with? Anything about the Pierron band in particular, the trip to New York? Did you remember? Oh yes, I can remember. When he first,

that I can recall that he remember, when he first left New Orleans in 1917, he left with Manuel Perez's band and they went to Chicago. I think it was at, I think Mike Fritz was the proprietor's name that they worked up there for. That was before Joe Oliver and them had gone up there. That was in 1917. And then that man was Perez, Lorenzo Teo, my father, Eddie Atkins, and Frankie Haney was playing piano. Well, he stayed there for about nine months and then he came and made a visit home on a vacation for two weeks and he went back. He came back in 1918. 1919, he went back again. He came back in 20. That was Manuel Perez again? Yeah, that was with Manuel Perez. Because Manuel stayed up there the whole time through. But my father, you know, he went and then came back. Then in 20 he came and he stayed and he went with John Robichaud again in the 20s. That's when they were working in the Lyric and he stayed there for about a year. Then he joined Pierron's band. They were working on the Spanish Foda at the time. And he stayed with the Pierron's band until the time of his death. In 1923, that's when they had gone up to New York.
